market.summary: Colombia offers high-leverage national, metropolitan and departmental public networks alongside large university systems and cajas de compensación libraries. Public registration/loan programmes, university eligibility and heritage room-use restrictions differ materially. This bounded check observes three PMB title-search successes, all reserves; the twelve major priorities remain blocked or unverified. It does not measure current national LMS share.
market.platform_strategy: Prioritize a policy-permitted Koha route/approved data arrangement for the largest cross-institution benefit, especially Antioquia/BiblioValle and university deployments. The 2021 academic study supports Koha as a common family; current OLIB-to-Koha migration and departmental deployment sources reinforce that direction. Janium is high leverage for Medellín/UPB but observed robots exclude all paths. Alma/Primo serves major networks but search and public frontend API paths are expressly excluded. PMB is the immediately evidenced technical reserve family, requiring deployment work and careful room-use semantics. Do not infer Sophia adoption: no Colombian institutional deployment was established.

network_opportunities.name: RNBP and departmental catalogues / Llave del Saber
network_opportunities.scope: National coordination plus distinct departmental/municipal collections
network_opportunities.verification: Official pages distinguish Koha services and Llave del Saber. BiblioValle 2025–2027 security plan describes Carvajal-hosted Koha/Llave integration. No national institution-specific holding was verified.
network_opportunities.integration_implication: Coordinate one Koha family where allowed; inspect returned holding ownership before any branch/institution expansion; identity/service system is not necessarily a single physical-books catalogue.

network_opportunities.name: Medellín public library shared Janium catalogue
network_opportunities.scope: Metropolitan public services and partners on rbmam.janium.net
network_opportunities.verification: Official page embeds observed Janium URL; robots excludes all paths.
network_opportunities.integration_implication: High public-reader reach but no allowed automated search verified; shared endpoints cannot justify counting each partner separately.

network_opportunities.name: Catálogo Colombia Discovery (OCLC)
network_opportunities.scope: Group catalogue of physical/electronic Colombian member-library collections
network_opportunities.verification: OCLC launch release 11 Dec 2025 establishes the service; membership/collection coverage and current title results were not independently tested.
network_opportunities.integration_implication: Potential high-leverage shared discovery route; requires exact institution holdings, coverage and permitted access validation. It is not a national union proof of live circulation or ten verified collections.

network_opportunities.name: Banco de la República / BLAA
network_opportunities.verification: Official guide identifies discovery across physical/electronic/digital material; Primo robots blocks search/API paths.
network_opportunities.integration_implication: One network integration can expose multiple cities, but separate physical holdings from digital licence access and retain membership conditions.

major_library_priorities.name: Biblioteca Nacional de Colombia
major_library_priorities.size_claim: More than two million publications; approximately 1.5 million newspapers/journals are separately described. Mixed media, not two million book titles.
major_library_priorities.outcome: Catalogue robots Disallow: /; no title request. SirsiDynix Symphony/Enterprise source evidence; heritage consultation.

limitations: No national largest-ten ranking established. Dates, record counts, mixed materials, physical copies, serial publications and digital licences are not comparable measures.
Zero of ten selected substantial targets verified; three smaller/specialized/unquantified PMB institutions are retained as reserves rather than padding the target.
Robots exclusions and bot challenges were respected. 404 robots is absence of a published policy, not permission or reuse licensing.
Only title forms and a single selected detail per successful institution were examined; no ISBN-search reliability, long-term health or application integration test.
All results are timestamped snapshots; past due dates retain on-loan status, and in-room consultation retains its restriction.
Search-engine-indexed official/vendor/study evidence supports marketplace and priorities but never counts as a successful live catalogue query.
Two origins for UNAL and two UdeA eras are documented as routes for the same institutions, not additional libraries.
